brief.brief: Examine whether open-weight models have genuinely closed the capability gap with leading closed models as of late 2026. Target reader: developers and product builders deciding which model tier to adopt for production features. Central point: benchmark leaderboards show convergence on specific tasks (coding, reasoning, instruction following) but persistent gaps remain in long-context reliability, tool use consistency, and safety alignment — differences that matter for product decisions. Useful concrete examples: compare recent releases such as Llama 3.1/3.2 family, Qwen 2.5, Nemotron 3 Ultra, and Mistral Large 2 against GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Gemini 1.5 Pro on public benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, LiveCodeBench, SWE-bench Verified, BFCL, HumanEval+) and note where evaluation methodology (prompt style, few-shot, agent scaffolding) changes rankings. Claims needing sources: current benchmark scores with dates, license terms for commercial use, context window and token pricing for API-served open models, and any independent replication of vendor-reported numbers.
